record.title: Brazil MGI issues advisory AI transparency guides for federal public services
record.summary: Brazil's Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services published two implementation guides for AI transparency in federal public services: an AI System Card for documenting system purposes, processing, limits and risks, and a Transparency Design Guide for notifying users when services use AI. The complete 37-page Design Guide v1.0 scopes recommendations to federal direct, autarchic and foundational administration and says it does not regulate AI uses or replace legal duties. MGI describes the wider self-assessment framework as orienting. Publication is established; agency uptake, binding effect and public-service outcomes are not.
organizations: Brazil Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Brazil's MGI published two AI transparency implementation guides on 2 July 2026, one for documenting AI systems and one for user-facing transparency design.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The 37-page Transparency Design Guide v1.0 covers digital interfaces and communications between federal public administration and citizens, and explicitly says it offers recommendations, does not regulate permitted or prohibited AI uses, and does not replace legal obligations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: MGI says the two guides support transparency guidance for more than 250 SISP bodies and are part of an orienting ethical-impact self-assessment framework.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed materials do not establish agency adoption, compliance, improved outcomes, or that the guides create binding duties.

evidence_gaps.description: The full AI System Card template is linked as DOCX, which the source reader could not fetch; only its official descriptive page was inspected.
No dated agency adoption, compliance evidence or public-service outcome was established.

brief.importance_rationale: If federal agencies use shared system-documentation and interface-disclosure guidance across public services, it could materially shape how public-sector AI is governed and experienced by citizens. The score reflects that potential consequence, not uptake or outcomes.
limitations: The ministry describes the self-assessment framework as orienting, and the complete Design Guide explicitly says it does not regulate AI uses or replace existing legal duties.
The System Card DOCX could not be retrieved through the available source reader.
No agency adoption, compliance, citizen understanding, service-quality, or outcome data was inspected.
The announcement page's 28 Oct update date has no description; event date remains 2 Jul 2026.
organizations: Brazil Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services

technical.claimed_result: MGI published an AI System Card and a Transparency Design Guide as implementation guidance for Brazil federal public services.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official announcement and complete 37-page Design Guide establish publication and scope. The Design Guide calls its recommendations non-regulatory and says it does not replace legal obligations.
technical.implementation_status: Guidance published; agency implementation was not established.
technical.mechanism: The materials pair lifecycle documentation of AI systems with risk-proportionate notices in citizen-facing digital interfaces and communications.
technical.regime: Brazilian federal direct, autarchic and foundational public administration, as scoped by the Design Guide.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable to a policy-guidance publication event; adoption and outcomes require separate evidence.
technical.strongest_baseline: Existing Brazilian legal duties and separate AI governance measures; the reviewed guides add non-binding implementation recommendations, with adoption not established.

brief.title: Brazil MGI issues advisory AI transparency guides for federal public services
brief.why_it_matters: Common guidance for documenting public-sector AI systems and disclosing AI use in federal services could affect how citizens understand and challenge government interactions if agencies adopt it. This records publication of advisory guidance, not adoption, compliance, or improved outcomes.
